title: RWB-P7-E1073-APP: the model answer, the dry-run report, the refusal of the model read, the workbook object, the version-list panel, the service login, the parameter codes and the physical registry columns are fixed by no source in the read set
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 14, 20, 27, 28, 41 and 43); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slides 11, 14, 15 and 16); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api rows, EV-30, JOB-20 and the table owners P7); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P7 Decision center and log v2.md (T3.1 defines decision_log_entry and approval only); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P7 Decision center and log v3.md (A2.1 to A2.8); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 073 Rule authoring validation test scenarios approval and rollback in Drools v1.md (sections 3, 11, 12, 13, 15 and 16)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 AC1, AC4, AC5, AC8 and AC10; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.3; 12.8; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages; 15 Screens and states
description: Several values this slice needs are given by no source in the read set, and each is written as a placeholder rather than a guess. (a) No source fixes the shape of the model answer of GET /rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 27 and Temporal and Drools design slide 15 name the path, the checksum verification and the swap, and say nothing about media type, whether the DRL, the compiled artefact or both travel, where the checksum sits, or whether the parsed catalogue rows ride in the same answer. (b) No source fixes the shape of the dry-run report beyond the legacy field names openCases, changedCases, byProduct, byQueue and byRule, and no source says whether it is nested maps or an array of triples. (c) No message identifier or text is written anywhere for the two refusals the split adds: a version that is not in force and a checksum that does not recompute. (d) No source names the file-store container, the document object or the claim-check identifier under which the target stores the workbook; the legacy story names a Blob container rule-packages with the path {packageCode}/{versionLabel}.xlsx, which is a monolith statement. (e) No source gives the panel or screen identifier of the version list in the target: the legacy story names no screen and SCR-39 Rules and parameters comes with Epic 8. (f) The per-service login name of DP-02 is stated as a pattern and not as a value, so the login of this service is not written out. (g) The catalog codes and the read path of the parameters rules.testcases.min (50) and drools.kiebase.cache.max (20) are given by no source, although DP-06 gives the owner of the parameter store. (h) The physical types, lengths and nullability of rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case are given by no source: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 defines decision_log_entry and approval and stops there. (i) No source lists the fields of RulePackageInForce beyond the facts the design names.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 names GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} as an accepted call and slide 27 gives the three steps load, verify checksum and swap in, with no payload; Temporal and Drools design slide 15 lists what a version stores (workbook in Blob, generated DRL, SHA-256, valid-from date, approver) and the six version states, with no wire shape; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 has decision_log_entry and approval and no registry table; the legacy story section 12 answers versionId, packageCode, versionLabel, status, validFrom, validTo, author, checksum, testResult {total, passed, failed, failedScenarioIds} and dryRunCounts {openCases, changedCases, byProduct, byQueue} on the six monolith paths and defines a DryRunReport of packageCode, versionLabel, evaluatedAt, openCases, changedCases, byProduct, byQueue and byRule; ownership.json carries owner P7 for rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case with a ruling and no fields.
owner_role: Service owner of rwb-decision with the solution architect and the API owner
proposed: Publish the registry resources in the rwb-decision contract with their physical columns and the model answer of GET /rule-models/{packageCode}/{version} (package code, version label, state, valid from, SHA-256, the DRL and the parsed catalogue rows in row order), the shape of the dry-run counts, the container and object name of the workbook, the panel identifier of the version list, the login of the service and the two parameter codes; until then the story and its fakes carry the shapes of ASM-B-P7-08-E1073-1 to ASM-B-P7-08-E1073-5.

title: RWB-P7-E1073-APP: the DP table adds eight platform H rows, one C row and one PLT object set that the metadata rows of the plan do not carry, and DP-04 points its C row at this service's own contract story
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (sections R5.4, R5.5 DP-03, DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-10, DP-14, DP-15, DP-19 and DP-09, and R5.7 rules 1 to 8); _work/msr/wp/B-P7-08.md (story line RWB-P7-E1073-APP: H [], C [RWB-P3-E1073-CON], patterns DP01 to DP19); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 20, 27 and 41); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slides 11, 15 and 16)
section: Metadata (Depends on (build); Contract dependencies); 3 Preconditions; 7 AC3 and AC8; 12.4; 12.7; 13 Pattern application
description: The DP table carries eight platform H rows, two C rows and one platform object set that no metadata row of the plan carries, and two of them conflict with the plan line. (a) The plan line gives Depends on (build) = None and Contract dependencies = RWB-P3-E1073-CON, while the DP table adds H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (DP-03), H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON (DP-04), H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and C RWB-P3-E1042-CON (DP-06), H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON (DP-07), H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (DP-10), H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON (DP-14), H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (DP-15) and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19): eight H rows and two C rows beyond the metadata. (b) DP-04 is the sharp case: its C row is RWB-P7-E1073-CON, a contract story of this service that the split plan does not carry (no CON slice of RWB-E1-073 exists for rwb-decision), so for this APP story the row is a self-reference and the governance seam is published here rather than consumed, while its H row is real because the compile check and the scenario runner call the embedded kit. (c) DP-09 is absent from this story's pattern list although the slice requires the outbox and inbox objects and this service publishes the promotion announcement; the objects are therefore read as a baseline prerequisite of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON. (d) H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON is the kit this story compiles and runs with, so the pattern row and the metadata row cannot both be complete as written.
evidence: WP B-P7-08 story line: H [], C [RWB-P3-E1073-CON], patterns [DP01, DP03, DP04, DP05, DP06, DP07, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP14, DP15, DP19]. Template and Rules R5.5: DP-03 adds H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-04 adds H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, DP-06 adds H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and C RWB-P3-E1042-CON, DP-07 adds H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON, DP-10 adds H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, DP-14 adds H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, DP-15 adds H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, DP-19 adds H RWB-PLT-N001-CON, DP-09 adds H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON. Architecture v5 slide 20 gives every service its own schema with outbox and inbox and names RulePackageInForce as a cache refresh; Temporal and Drools design slides 15 and 16 put the compile, the checksum and the KieBase in the kit.
owner_role: Solution architect with the platform library owner and the rwb-decision service owner
proposed: Either complete the metadata rows from the DP table (eight H rows and the one C row of DP-06 and DP-07) and add DP-09 to the pattern list, or state in R5.5 that a platform H and a self-referential C are held by the platform story and the contract story and are not repeated on the APP line; until then the story keeps the plan's rows and reads the DP rows as dependencies added by the patterns, as its section 13 states.

title: RWB-P7-E1073-APP: the same rule registry is named as /admin/rule-versions by API Specification v4 and the integration story and as /admin/rule-package* by the legacy story and the Ownership Map, and a third read /rule-catalog is consumed but unowned
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R4, R5.5 DP-13); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (the six /admin/rule-package* rows, owner P7, ruling ASM-A6-api-3); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 14 and 27); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 073 Rule authoring validation test scenarios approval and rollback in Drools v1.md (section 12); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-ITG-W1 Wave 1 integration/RWB ITG E1073 ITG Rule authoring, validation, test scenarios, approval and rollback in Drools - integration v1.md (sections 3, 12.2 and 12.4); _work/msr/fragments/RWB-P3-E1073-CON.json (the seven consumed decision operations)
description: The inventory spells the registry two ways and carries a third read with no owner. (a) API Specification v4, and RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG which reads it, give the registry as GET and POST /admin/rule-versions, POST /admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve and POST /admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/rollback, and say in terms that the legacy /admin/rule-packages family has no target under that name. (b) The legacy story and the six Ownership Map rows give the same registry as /admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions, /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve, /rollback and /dry-run, all attributed to P7 with the ruling ASM-A6-api-3. (c) RWB-P3-E1073-CON consumes a seventh operation, GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion=, which appears in no Ownership Map row and in no API Specification inventory. (d) The two spellings cannot both be served: one registry answering two names would make the version a caller reads depend on which document it followed, and the integration story and the contract story would each hold a fake of a different surface. This story publishes the /admin/rule-package* family because it is the family the Ownership Map attributes and serves no path under /admin/rule-versions; the parsed catalogue is served inside the model answer and no separate catalogue path is published.
evidence: API Specification v4 x-module P7 and RWB-ITG-E1073-ITG section 12.2 list GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-versions and the three /admin/rule-versions/{versionId} actions, and section 12.2 ends by saying that the legacy /admin/rule-packages paths have no target under those names; ownership.json lists GET /admin/rule-packages, POST and GET /admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions, POST /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve, /rollback and GET /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/dry-run with owner P7; RWB-E1-073 section 12 writes the same six paths on the monolith base; RWB-P3-E1073-CON.json ops_consumed lists GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion= as a consumed operation with no provider.
owner_role: Solution architect with the API owner and the rwb-decision service owner
proposed: Fix one family for the registry in API Specification v4 and the Ownership Map before the wave-1 contract baseline is tagged, restate the integration story and the contract story on it, and either publish GET /rule-catalog as a seventh owned operation or remove it from the consumed set and state that the catalogue travels with the model answer.

title: RWB-P7-E1073-APP: the case read that feeds the dry run is attributed to RWB-P3-E1073-CON by the plan and to RWB-P3-E1023-CON by the P3 contract story, which serves no operation
source: _work/msr/wp/B-P7-08.md (the slice: the dry run against open cases read through the RWB-P3-E1073-CON contract); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P3 rwb-case (Case and workflow)/RWB P3 E1073 CON Rule authoring, validation, test scenarios, approval and rollback in Drools - contract v1.md (section 12.1 states None and attributes the case read to RWB-P3-E1023-CON); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P3 rwb-case (Case and workflow)/RWB P3 E1073 APP Rule authoring, validation, test scenarios, approval and rollback in Drools v1.md (section 12.1); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P7 Decision center and log v2.md (T-A.1)
description: The plan gives this story one contract dependency, RWB-P3-E1073-CON, and names it as the contract through which the dry run reads the open cases. The P3 contract story of that identifier states in section 12.1 that it serves no business operation at all, that the case fact mapping is internal and the scenario gate runs in the pipeline, and that the case read belongs to RWB-P3-E1023-CON. Read literally, this story would hold a contract dependency that publishes nothing it needs, and the dry run would read a path owned by a story it does not depend on. Two readings follow: either RWB-P3-E1073-CON is the seam of the whole rule-authoring conversation and its fakes carry the case answers this story calls, or the metadata dependency should have been RWB-P3-E1023-CON. The story reads the case through the P3 seam the plan names, fakes both answers of section 12.8 on Day 1, and cites the second story in section 12.2 so a reader is not misled.
evidence: WP B-P7-08 slice text and story line C [RWB-P3-E1073-CON]; RWB-P3-E1073-CON section 12.1: None, with the case read attributed to GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} of RWB-P3-E1023-CON and unchanged by that story; RWB-P3-E1073-APP section 12.1 repeats the same attribution; TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 carries no case read for P7; the legacy story section 11 reads the five case fields through the P3 repository.
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-case contract owner and the rwb-decision service owner
proposed: State in RWB-P3-E1073-CON whether it publishes the case reads its consumers need, or move this story's contract dependency to the P3 story that does; until then the story reads the case through the P3 contract it was given and fakes both answers.

title: RWB-P7-E1073-APP: REFUSED is one of the six version states while a load refused at a check writes no rule_package_version row, so no stored version ever reaches it
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slide 15: version states LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 27 and 28); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 073 Rule authoring validation test scenarios approval and rollback in Drools v1.md (sections 4, 5 X12 and AC13: no rule_package_version row is written and no Blob object is stored); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (rule_package_version owner P7)
section: 5 Exception paths; 7 AC2 and AC7; 9 State transitions; 11 Data
description: The design names six states a rule package version can hold, and the legacy story refuses a bad load without writing a version row at all, so a refused load never has a row to carry REFUSED. Both statements are right where they stand and together they leave one value of the state list unreachable. Either REFUSED is a state of a stored version refused later in its life, or a refused load must write a version row marked REFUSED, which contradicts the rule that a refused load leaves nothing behind and would make the version list of a package grow with every bad workbook anybody uploads. This story takes the first reading: a refused load writes no row and is proved by its decision log entry, and REFUSED is written only on the night of promotion when a stored APPROVED version fails its recompiled check or its checksum. The reading changes no business value and no message, and it is recorded so that the state list and the refusal rule can be reconciled in one place.
evidence: Temporal and Drools design slide 15 notes: Version states: LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED; RWB-E1-073 section 4 step 8 refuses the load whole, section 5 row X12 says no rule_package_version row is written and no Blob object is stored, and AC13 repeats it; RWB-E1-073 section 9 lists REFUSED in the state table as the outcome of a failed load.
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-decision service owner
proposed: State in the design that REFUSED is a state of a stored version that failed its promotion checks, and that a load refused at a check leaves no version row and is proved by its decision log entry; or add a REFUSED version row to the load and say what it contains.

title: Envelope and payload element names of DecisionRecorded, and the shape of the inputs snapshot
source: Architecture v5 slides 20, 28 and 42 row 08; Temporal and Drools design slide 11 and slide 16; TSD P7 T3.1 (decision_log_entry); FSD P7 A2.2 and A2.3; RWB-P2-E2001-CON 12.3 and 12.5
description: No source fixes how the hand-over facts travel inside DecisionRecorded. The story therefore records as assumed the element names that carry the business date, the queue and owner identifiers of the hand-over, the hand-over reference and the actions payload, the shape of the inputs snapshot that holds the ACE business date 2026-12-14, and the composite key by which the second dedupe on case and business date is expressed in decision_log_entry.idempotency_key. The two dedupe keys, the chain columns and the required entry fields are fixed by TSD P7 T3.1 and Arch v5 slide 28; only their carrier in the event and the snapshot is open. The hand-over contract of RWB-P2-E2001-CON also publishes no summary operation, because its HandoverSummary is an activity answer, so no hand-over summary path is available to consume and none is invented.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 42 row 08 names DecisionRecorded, its producer and its topic only. TSD P7 T3.1 gives inputs_ref as a varchar(400) reference to the inputs snapshot with the freshness of each input and names no element inside it. RWB-P2-E2001-CON 12.1 states that the step provides no summary endpoint and 12.5 fixes HandoverSummary as an activity output; its 12.3 leaves the physical names to the review with each owner.
area: Event contract and decision record payload
proposed: Fix the DecisionRecorded payload and the inputs snapshot in the event contract of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and the AsyncAPI document of rwb.decision-record.v1, with the business date, the queue and owner identifiers of the hand-over, the hand-over reference, the actions and the composite idempotency key, and confirm it with the hand-over contract owner before the wave 2 build.

title: Answer field set and business-date filter of the decision-log read, and the screen that shows an entry beside the case
source: TSD P7 appendix T-A API-P7-006 and API-P7-007; API Specification v4 (/decision-log); FSD P7 A2.28, the screens list and Appendix B; Arch v5 slide 14 (rwb-decision OUT)
description: The TSD fixes the filters caseId, decision, ruleId, approver, from, to, page and size, and the API Specification adds chainVerified on each item and the warning MSG-P7-012, but no source fixes a business-date filter parameter, the remaining fields of DecisionLogPage and DecisionLogEntry, the page-size limit of this read or the screen or panel identifier that shows a decision entry beside the case. The story therefore writes the business-date filter as the query parameter businessDate, records only chainVerified as an added answer field, and leaves the panel identifier open rather than reusing the interaction timeline panel of another owner.
evidence: TSD P7 API-P7-006 lists the eight filters and answers DecisionLogPage; API Specification v4 states that the read adds chainVerified and carries MSG-P7-012 when an entry fails the chain. The FSD P7 screens list gives SCR-38 Decision log query for the search but names no panel that shows an entry beside the case, and its SCR-03 reference in A2.28 describes the interaction history panel, which is the P1 ledger's and not this read's.
proposed: Add the business-date filter, the full answer field set and the page-size limit to the decision-log contract, and name one screen or panel for a decision entry beside the case, in consultation with the audit query story and the gateway-bff route owner.

title: Per-service login of rwb_decision, the chain-check workflow and activity names, and the Schedule identifier of JOB-14
source: Architecture v5 slides 14, 20, 29 and 44; Temporal and Drools design slides 11 and 16; Plan DP-02 and DP-10; TSD P7 T1 and T2

The story therefore names the workflow LedgerChainCheckWorkflow with the activities readDayEntries, verifyChain and reportBreak, registers JOB-14 as a Temporal Schedule at 02:00 in queue rwb-decision and takes the login from the platform database story as an assumed value.

title: Shape of the model answer, of the inputs snapshot and of the announcement, with the carrier names of the plan-status move
source: Architecture v5 slides 14, 20, 27 and 28; Temporal and Drools design slides 11, 15 and 16; TSD P7 T3.1 (decision_log_entry) and appendix T-A API-P7-006; FSD P7 A2.1, A2.2 and A2.3; RWB-P2-E2002-CON 12.1
description: No source fixes the physical shape of the answer of the model operation beyond the version label and the SHA-256, the shape of the inputs snapshot of a plan-status move, or the element names that carry the plan reference, the plan status, its date and the route state inside the DecisionRecorded envelope and the actions payload. The story therefore writes as assumed: the model answer as a JSON envelope carrying the package code, the version label, the SHA-256, the in-force time and the compiled artifact as the claim-check of the version; the inputs snapshot as a reference naming the plan reference, the plan status and its date, the route state, the break count, the prior route and the freshness of the plan read; the business date as an envelope element and the plan facts as keys of the actions payload; the per-service login of DP-02 as the phrase the rwb_decision login; the page size of the read as 50; and the entry panel as the plan-status section of SCR-38, taken from the sibling harness story. The texts of the messages this story raises are the legacy texts, and the chain-break text is the one RWB-P7-E1020-APP carries, so no message text is invented and no new identifier is coined. The sources that do fix values are respected: the chain columns, the required entry fields and the three field groups are fixed by TSD P7 T3.1 and FSD P7 AC-ALT-P7-001-02, the version states by Temporal and Drools slide 15, and the plan-status operation of rwb-integration by RWB-P2-E2002-CON.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 27 names GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} and a checksum but no answer shape; slide 28 fixes the record, its transaction and its chain and names no element; API-P7-006 lists eight query filters and answers DecisionLogPage without a field list. TSD P7 T3.1 gives inputs_ref as a varchar(400) reference with the freshness of each input and names no element inside it, and FSD P7 A2.14 lists the entry fields without the plan facts. RWB-P2-E2002-CON 12.1 fixes planRef, accountNo, status, statusDate, live and messageCode and says nothing of how the record of the move carries them.
area: REST answer, event payload and screen
proposed: Fix the model answer, the inputs snapshot and the announcement payload in the registry contract of RWB-P7-E1073-CON and the record envelope of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, name the plan-status section of the decision log screen with the gateway-bff route owner, and publish the per-service login with the database platform story, before the wave 2 build.

title: One ledger entry per route move or per case and business date, for a move that runs two rules
source: Legacy RWB-E2-002 AC2 and section 9; FSD P7 AC-P7-002-01 and AC-ALT-P7-001-02; TSD P7 T3.1 DF-DEC-031; Architecture v5 slide 28; RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG AC2
description: The legacy story writes a decision log entry for each move, and its plan-status move moves the route state twice in one transaction, from PLAN_CURE_PERIOD to PLAN_BROKEN by R-RES-29 and then to BACK_TO_ROUTE_DECISION by R-RES-30, so the same case and business date carry two rules. The ledger key of the target is one entry per case and business date with the rule identity in the dedupe, and FSD P7 shows two entries for one case and one date when two decisions are taken. No source settles whether the two rule steps of one move are one entry with the second rule in its actions or two entries of the same date.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-002 AC2 states that a decision log entry is written for each move with the rule ID and the package version, and its section 9 gives the two transitions. proposed: Settle in the ledger contract of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON whether a route move that runs two rules is one entry with the second rule in its actions or two entries of the date, and make the harness of RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG and the case story follow the same answer.

title: rwb-decision credit approval slice: the decide path, the delegation answer shape, the actions keys, the comparison site, the message texts, the decision sub-code, the per-service login and the screen identity are not fixed by any one source
source: WP B-P7-08; legacy RWB-E2-006 sections 1 to 19; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1, A2.2, A2.4, A2.5, A2.15, A2.16, A2.19, A2.21, A2.24, A2.25 and appendices A and B; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1, T3.2 and appendix T-A; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 20, 27, 28, 41 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 6, 11, 14 and 16; Ownership Map v1
description: One combined gap covers every value of this slice that no single source fixes. (1) The rwb-decision login of DP-02 is given nowhere; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery_svc login and the story names the login by role until the name is agreed. (2) The path that writes the D5 entry is named twice differently: Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-decision the input POST /approvals/{id}/decide and the TSD appendix T-A gives the approve, return and refuse paths of the same resource, while the Ownership Map API catalogue holds GET /approvals, GET /approvals/{approvalId} and the three action paths but no decide path; the request and answer field names of ApprovalAction and DecisionLogEntry are not written out. (3) The shape of the delegation read is not fixed: the Ownership Map cites API Specification v3 GET /doa-limits for P4 but the catalogue has no row for that path for any service, so the query parameters, the answer fields, the name of the level element and the meaning of the NOT_COVERED answer are assumed. (4) Whether the comparison of the level the result carries against the level the delegation sets is made in rwb-decision or in the calling service is not fixed by any source: the legacy comparison ran in process in one module, FSD P7 A2.24 makes the level read a P7 feature that records the version used, and the P2 and P3 slices of the same key each hold their own comparison. (5) How the NLEADS reference, the approval level, the required level and the result date travel from the caller and in the envelope of rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 is not fixed; TSD T3.1 has no column for them, so they are written in the actions payload and the key names are assumed, and the entry's idempotency key shape is assumed with them. (6) Several message ids are named but never written out: MSG-P7-010 is named in FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-015-06, AC-EXC-P7-019-06 and AC-EXC-P7-024-04 as the incident of a request no delegation row covers but no text is given, and MSG-GEN-006 is a platform message whose wording this slice does not hold. (7) The FSD field catalog of the decision code lists D5.1 to D9.3 as the values of LOV-DECISION while the legacy story writes the family code D5, and which of the two the credit entry carries is not stated. (8) The screen or panel identity on which the credit entries are read is not fixed: SCR-38 Decision log query is the service's own screen and SCR-14 Treatment record is the pack's, and no source says whether the credit entries appear on the panel of SCR-14. (9) The legacy criteria carry two different approval levels for the same case: the Background of RWB-E2-006 and its AC7 set the plan at level L6 or higher under item 2.1.1, its AC2 records level L5 on the same case and expects the result to be accepted, and the P2 and P3 slices of this key copy both unchanged. The delegation returns L6 for item 2.1.1, MORTGAGE and 2,400,000.00 baht under DOA-2026.11 and L5 for the same case from 1 January 2027 under DOA-2027.01 (FSD P7 AC-ALT-P7-024-01 and AC-ALT-P7-024-02; Temporal and Drools slide 6), so this story accepts a result at L6 and uses L5 for the below-level refusal, while the legacy criteria keep their own values with their owning slices.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-006 section 3 (recovery_svc login, the checklist items CREDIT_APPLICATION, ID_COPY, TITLE_DEED, LATEST_APPRAISAL and INCOME_PROOF, the 1 business day input age limit under DL22), section 12 (DelegationQuery.requiredLevel, DecisionLogWriter.write, the CreditPack and CreditResult shapes, If-Match), section 14 (MSG-P7-003, MSG-P7-006, MSG-P2-010, MSG-P2-018, MSG-P3-005, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002, MSG-GEN-004, MSG-P4-002) and section 15 (SCR-14); FSD P7 A2.16.3.2 and A2.21.3.2 field catalog (decision_code D5.1 to D9.3, inputs_ref, recommendation), A2.24.4.3 AC-EXC-P7-024-01 to AC-EXC-P7-024-05 (MSG-P7-010 and NOT_COVERED), A2.15.4.3 AC-EXC-P7-015-06 (HELD_NO_LIMIT, MSG-P7-010), A2.5 (MSG-P7-003, principle 5) and the screens table (SCR-38 Decision log query); TSD P7 T3.1 (decision_log_entry DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031, approval DF-DEC-032 to DF-DEC-053), T3.2 (LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL L1 to L6, LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS WAITING, HELD_NO_LIMIT, APPROVED, REFUSED, RETURNED) and appendix T-A API-P7-002 to API-P7-008; Architecture v5 slide 14 (P7 IN POST /approvals/{id}/decide and GET /decisions?caseId=, OUT schema rwb_decision approvals and central decision ledger, REST Access: DoA limits), slide 20 (DecisionRecorded to rwb.decision-record.v1), slide 27 and slide 28 (local record, sealed centrally); Ownership Map v1 (decision_log_entry and approval owner P7, delegation_limit owner P4, GET /decision-log and GET /decision-log/{entryId} owner P7, no doa-limits row in the api catalogue); Temporal and Drools slide 14 RecordAndApply note and slide 11 (one transaction of state, record and outbox); legacy RWB-E2-006 Background (the plan needs level L6 or higher under item 2.1.1), AC2 (level L5 recorded on the same case) and AC7 (level L6 refused for a plan that needs L5); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 6 (L6 under DOA-2026.11 and L5 under DOA-2027.01 for the same 2,400,000.00 baht case)
proposed: Settle in the wave 2 contract review with the rwb-access, rwb-integration and rwb-case contract owners: the rwb-decision login name with the ACE DB owner; which path serves the credit decision on the approval resource, with the request and answer field names of ApprovalAction and DecisionLogEntry; the operation, query and answer shape of the delegation read, with its catalogue row; one owner for the level comparison, so that the caller's guard and this service's refusal cannot disagree; the key names that carry the NLEADS reference, the levels and the result date in the actions payload and in the rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1 envelope; the text of MSG-P7-010 and the platform wording of MSG-GEN-006; whether the entry carries D5 or one of the D5.1 to D9.3 sub-codes; the level the accepted result of the 2026-12-17 case carries, since the legacy criteria record L5 on a case their own Background sets at L6; and the screen the credit entries are read on. Record the outcome in the contract stories and in the gap and assumption registers; no business value changes in this story.

title: The platform and published dependencies this slice adds through the decoupling patterns are not carried by the empty metadata rows
source: WP B-P7-08 story object for RWB-P7-E2006-APP (H, C, I and X empty); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP table and section R5.7; section 13 pattern application of this story
description: The story object fixes Depends on (build), Contract dependencies, Integration dependencies and External dependencies empty, and the metadata rows are copied that way. The patterns this story applies add dependencies that no metadata row carries: DP-03 adds the platform decision-record contract RWB-PLT-E1027-CON as an H row; DP-07 adds the platform reference-data contract RWB-PLT-E1043-CON as an H row and the rwb-case reference-data contract RWB-P3-E1043-CON as a C row; DP-11 adds the C row of the legacy delegation dependency, which is the rwb-access contract RWB-P4-E1037-CON that publishes the delegation level, and it is the one contract this story cannot be built or contract-tested without; DP-15 adds RWB-PLT-E1044-CON as an H row and DP-19 adds RWB-PLT-N001-CON as an H row. evidence: WP B-P7-08 story object for RWB-P7-E2006-APP (H [], C [], I [], X []); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 rows DP-03 (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON), DP-07 (H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON), DP-11 (none, C from the legacy dependency), DP-15 (H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON) and DP-19 (H RWB-PLT-N001-CON); section R5.7 rule 2 and rule 3; RWB-P7-E2006-APP sections 3, 7, 12.2, 12.8 and 13; Ownership Map v1 (delegation_limit owner P4; the DoA limit read is a P7 outbound call on Architecture v5 slide 14)

title: The delegation of authority table is ruled to rwb-access by the Ownership Map while the integration story of this key attributes the required level to rwb-decision
source: Ownership Map v1 table delegation_limit and the rulings list; WP B-P7-08; RWB-ITG-E2006-ITG section 1 and section 19; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.24; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 6; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41
description: Two sources disagree on who owns the delegation of authority table. The Ownership Map rules delegation_limit to P4 rwb-access, on Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41, TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and API Specification v3 GET /doa-limits, and states in the ruling that the versioned reference-data wording of the Drools design does not move the table to P3. The integration story of this same legacy key instead describes its third owning slice as the required level from the delegation of authority and the D5 decision record, and its out-of-scope list leaves the delegation table to P4 while expecting rwb-decision to hold the level, which reads as an attribution of the level to P7. FSD P7 A2.24 is written as a P7 feature that reads the limits from the versioned table and records the version used, and Temporal and Drools slide 6 says delegation limits are held as versioned reference data with the same approve-and-date discipline as the rule packages, which points at a P7 or P3 owner. The API catalogue of the Ownership Map has no row for the DoA limit read at all, so nothing in that section settles the question. This story resolves it the only way the higher sources allow: the table stays P4's, and the level is read through the contract of the owner, RWB-P4-E1037-CON, with no table read, no copy of the rows, no level in code and no claim on delegation_limit in section 12.7. The disagreement is recorded here so that the next reader of the ITG slice, FSD A2.24 and the Ownership Map ruling is not left with two answers.
evidence: Ownership Map v1: delegation_limit owner P4, basis Architecture v5 slide 41 P4 (DoA table) and slide 14 P4 DB line, TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and API Specification v3 GET /doa-limits x_module P4, ruling ASM-A6-tables-4 and the rulings list row delegation_limit; RWB-ITG-E2006-ITG section 1 (RWB-P7-E2006-APP holds the required level from the delegation of authority and the D5 decision record) and section 19 (the five owning stories); FSD P7 A2.24.1 intent and A2.24.4.2 AC-ALT-P7-024-01 and AC-ALT-P7-024-02 (lookup returns level L6 or L5 with the row and the version in force); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 6 note (delegation limits are held as versioned reference data, delegation_limit, following the rule-package approve-and-date discipline); Architecture v5 slide 14 (P7 OUT REST Access: DoA limits; P4 OUT schema rwb_access with the DoA table) and slide 41 (P4 owns the DoA table)
proposed: Confirm in the wave 2 ownership review that delegation_limit stays with P4 rwb-access and that rwb-decision holds only the level it read and the version it applied, as the Ownership Map ruling already states; correct the attribution in the ITG story and in any story that reads the level, and add the DoA limit read to the Ownership Map API catalogue with P4 as its owner and P7, P3 and P2 as its consumers. If the ruling is overturned, this story gains the table and loses the RWB-P4-E1037-CON read, and the change is a contract and data change only, with no business value moved.
